newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PLA soldiers get low key welcome but harbour views.
newsitem.headline: PLA soldiers get low key welcome but harbour views.

text.p: China's advance troops slipped into Hong Kong with little fanfare on Monday, taking up residence in the heart of the British colony with harbour views and surrounded by some the world's most expensive real estate.

Martial strains accompanied the 40-strong contingent of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) as it left to cross the land border into Hong Kong to prepare for the territory's return to China at midnight on June 30.
But the soldiers found a low key welcome as they completed the 30 km (20 mile) drive to the Prince of Wales Barracks beside the world's busiest harbour.

Military police in khaki uniforms and red hats and troops in camouflage uniforms and green berets stood by as the unit arrived. In the yard, a handful of men in kilts from Britain's Black Watch regiment milled around.
There was none of the regiment's traditional bagpipe performances, no bands playing, no bunting. Just a low key reception with routine military courtesies.
British garrison commander Major-General Bryan Dutton exchanged salutes and handshakes with China's Major-General Zhou Borong before leading his party into the barracks.

"I am delighted to welcome Major-General Zhou Borong and his advance party to the British garrison in Hong Kong and to the Prince of Wales Barracks," Dutton said, standing on the steps under a hazy, overcast sky.

"We intend to ensure that the garrison gives the PLA every possible assistance in their preparations," he said, competing with the rumble of construction sites and traffic noise that form a 24-hour backdrop to life in Hong Kong.

The PLA unit drove up to the barracks in an eight vehicle convoy, shortly after the British garrison's annual 21 gun salute in honour of Queen Elizabeth's birthday was fired from the warship HMS Starling, anchored nearby.
The PLA's job is to prepare garrison facilities, logistical arrangements and communications for the territory's return to China and the eventual presence of up to 10,000 Chinese troops.

A British spokeswoman said there would be meetings between the PLA and the British to discuss arrangements for the Chinese troops, 28 of whom will be billeted at the barracks while 12 will be stationed at a base on nearby Stonecutters' Island.
"This is the first time the PLA have been on Hong Kong soil," she said. "Our guiding principle is to be as helpful as possible."
"It's interesting," Sergeant Paul Keenan said of the arrival of the communist troops. "It's a thing to tell your kids about when you're older."
The PLA will move into apartments in the top-security Prince of Wales complex, which stands on the shores of Victoria Harbour in the shadow of Hong Kong's tallest skyscapers.

The barracks, the centre of British defence in Hong Kong, includes a HK$82 million (US$10.6 million) office building, residential blocks, a swimming pool, officers' messes and other facilities that the PLA will get after the handover.
Mechanical diggers and workmen have torn up the land perimeter and filled in the former naval basin, now a parade ground that will be used for handover ceremonials.
Painters and decorators have worked for weeks to give the complex a facelift with fresh white paint for the final few weeks of British rule.
However, the advance party is not getting VIP facilities.
"We are handing over standard military accommodation to them," a spokesman said.

But if the way to a soldier's heart is through his stomach, they will at least be getting a familiar cuisine. Brand new Chinese-style cooking facilities have been set up for the unit, complete with large Chinese woks, or frying pans.
